[1/3] Report a test-tier timeout as a clean, actionable failure and give verify_commit per-gate timeouts so the tiers gate can finish its own bound

impact_assessment.why: verify_commit.py reported the tiers gate as failed on commit aac4336 with a raw subprocess.TimeoutExpired traceback: scripts/check_test_budgets.py runs each tier with subprocess.run(timeout=300) and never catches the timeout, so a tier that overruns under host load crashes the gate instead of reporting it. The same commit's 786 tests pass in a clean worktree, so the gate, not the code, was the failing surface.
impact_assessment.benefits: A timed-out tier becomes a named [FAIL] with its own Why and Fix, exit 1, and no traceback; the 300s bound becomes an explicit hang detector rather than an accidental load limit; verify_commit gives the three-tier gate room to reach that clean report instead of being killed by one outer 600s cap shared with single-script gates.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: check_test_budgets gains a timeout result state and verify_commit's gate table gains a timeout column, both internal to their modules; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: another session is editing scripts/project_media.py and tests/test_kit.py in this tree, so only the two script files are edited until its work is committed and explicit staging excludes it; state: none beyond stdout and exit codes
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first unit tests for a timeout runner double and for a per-gate timeout table; keep the injected 2-argument runner contract; re-read tests/test_kit.py before writing and stage only my own hunks after the other session's edits are gone; both tiers plus every read-only gate before any commit
